transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Solutions); Samir (Aurora Head of Platform), Daphne (ML Eng), Carlos (Security)

Summary:
Quick integration discovery covering SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Aurora is evaluating hosted first but wants options for Dedicated/Private for compliance. Next steps include sharing integration examples, pricing, and scheduling a technical benchmark.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain connectors, LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy architecture, per-route rate limits & quotas, observability / OpenTelemetry hooks, security (SSO/KMS/VPC), benchmarking plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and this is Arjun our systems engineer and Lina on solutions. you all good on time?
[00:12] Samir: Yep, works for us. thanks for doing this.
[00:15] Arjun: Quick agenda — talk integration surface area, what SDKs you use, existing vector store or LlamaIndex, gateway questions, and then security/ops hooks. then we'll pick follow ups. sound good?
[00:22] Daphne: Sounds great. High level — we're building an assistant product for enterprise customers; currently using a mix of in-house embedding service and some open-source models for experimentation. primary concerns are latency, cost, and data residency.
[00:36] Carlos: and from security perspective we need SSO, audit logs, KMS integration, and the option for Private or VPC-delivered deployments.
[00:44] Maya: Totally. So quick call-outs: Redwood offers Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads. For integration we support Python and Node SDKs and official connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. we also have a gateway pattern if you want a proxy layer.
[01:05] Daphne: When you say connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, is that maintained upstream or a Redwood shim?
[01:12] Arjun: Good question — we maintain official connectors/examples in our SDK repo; many customers use LangChain's provider interface with small adapter bits, and LlamaIndex integrations are available as example notebooks. sometimes Lang Chain spelling in their docs gets a little off, but we keep the adapters current.
[01:29] Daphne: ok good. Our stack uses LangChain in python heavily and a clickhouse-backed vector DB, and we use streaming responses for UX. any specifics about streaming and token limits?
[01:40] Arjun: Streaming is supported in both SDKs — you can get chunked server-sent events or websockets. token limits depend on model variant; hosted defaults have per-request token caps we expose in the model catalog. For Dedicated, we can customize the token window and session timeouts. Also we do prefix/KV cache to speed repeated context.
[02:05] Samir: about gateway/proxy — we currently route requests through our API gateway. do customers typically call Redwood directly or do you recommend a sidecar/reverse-proxy?
[02:15] Maya: Both patterns are used. Many teams call Redwood directly with short-lived API tokens (rotate via your identity system). For tighter control we've seen two patterns: 1) customer-side gateway that authenticates and forwards; 2) Redwood sidecar deployed in your VPC that maps internal routes to model variants — that second is common for Private/Dedicated setups.
[02:35] Carlos: if we go Private, can we bring our own HSM/KMS?
[02:40] Arjun: Yes — for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping, and you keep control of encryption keys. We also support KMIP-compatible stores in some on-prem configs.
[02:52] Daphne: any friction integrating with LlamaIndex embeddings — we use LlamaIndex's vector store API with annoy/faiss backends — do you have a recommended flow?
[03:02] Arjun: The typical flow is offline embedding generation via our embeddings endpoint, store vectors in your DB, then use either LlamaIndex or LangChain chains to call generation endpoints. We have code samples: python snippet for batch embedding, and a streaming example for chat chains. If you want, we can share a Jupyter with your vector store specifics.
[03:24] Samir: how about rate limits and quotas — per-api-key or per-route? we need per-customer quotas inside our app.
[03:30] Maya: Redwood supports rate limiting at multiple layers: per API key, per model-route, and account-level quotas. For Hosted customers we also offer soft quotas with warning webhooks; Dedicated gives you stronger QoS and configurable per-tenant limits. For fine-grained internal quotas inside your app, most customers implement a local gateway that maps your internal tenant IDs to Redwood API keys and enforces per-tenant quotas.
[03:56] Daphne: and what about throttling behavior? is there a 429 with retry-after?
[04:01] Arjun: Yes — we return standard 429 plus Retry-After header. We also provide backpressure guidance and a client-side retry helper in the SDK. For high-throughput workloads we recommend batching and the 2-phase warmup for KV cache to avoid cold-start latency.
[04:20] Carlos: observability — can we get tracing hooks into our existing OpenTelemetry pipeline? we need per-request latency traces and per-token cost attribution.
[04:29] Arjun: We emit traces and expose OpenTelemetry-compatible spans. You can push traces to your APM. The Console provides per-route token/latency breakdowns and model-level dashboards. We can also ship trace hooks to append a request id so you can join logs across services. Token-level cost is exported as metrics in the console and via our usage API.
[04:52] Samir: any gotchas around streaming with OpenTelemetry?
[04:56] Arjun: Slight — streaming spans can be minimized to a single request span with child events for chunks; we provide best-practice instrumentation examples.
[05:06] Daphne: one technical ask — we use LangChain's agents heavily and sometimes call model tool-calls. does Redwood support function/tool calling and structured output?
[05:15] Arjun: Yes. function/tool calling is supported — we return structured JSON and have schema enforcement options. For safety, you can set strict output parsing or fall back to a raw text stream.
[05:26] Maya: quick commercial note — hosted is easiest to start, Dedicated is the middle ground with reserved capacity pricing, and Private is for regulated customers. We can show a TCO comparison once we see your request volume and sequence length distributions.
[05:40] Samir: we're leaning hosted for a pilot but need a clear migration path to Dedicated/Private if customers require it.
[05:47] Maya: totally reasonable, we do that a lot. we'll outline migration steps in the docs we'll share.
[05:53] Daphne: question on data retention and logs: do you keep user-level transcripts? can we opt in/out per-route?
[06:00] Arjun: By default hosted has configurable retention windows; enterprise tiers give you longer retention and audit logs. We also support redact-on-ingest patterns and can disable transcript retention for sensitive routes. On Private you control retention entirely.
[06:16] Carlos: for compliance we need SOC2 + ISO plus evidence for key rotation and access logs, is that packaged?
[06:21] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts for customers; we'll attach our compliance pack. For Private customers we also do architecture reviews and provide runbooks for key rotation and access controls.
[06:35] Daphne: are there existing customers using LangChain + Redwood in production? any references?
[06:40] Lina: we have several anonymized case studies and an example repo with LangChain integrations we can share.
[06:47] Samir: price sensitivity — what about unit cost for embeddings vs generation?
[06:52] Maya: embeddings and generations are priced differently; we usually show per-1k token and per-embedding unit rates. we'll include a sample cost spreadsheet for your workload.
[07:02] Daphne: for the benchmark, we can produce a sample of 10k requests with typical prompt sizes; would you run it against hosted and Dedicated?
[07:09] Arjun: yes we can run both. for Dedicated we'll need the expected concurrency and sequence length to size the pool; for hosted we can run a bucketed test to show colder and warmer KV cache behavior.
[07:22] Carlos: last question: SSO for our team — is SAML supported for console/portal?
[07:27] Maya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning are supported on enterprise plans.
[07:33] Samir: Ok this is helpful — next steps?
[07:36] Maya: recap: we'll send integration guide + connectors repo, Dedicated/Private pricing and SLA one-pager, sample cost spreadsheet, and schedule a SE deep-dive/benchmark.
[07:47] Daphne: sounds good, we'll also send the sample dataset and expected request shapes.
[07:52] Maya: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and a calendar for the benchmark.
[07:58] Samir: thanks, bye.
[08:00] End call.
